description:
FILED s507 (Fable, 2026-10-04) from review probes written for s502e (#2537 list-valued `use constant`).  PRE-EXISTING on main 2e71d4aa; s502e's #2537 fix (a comma list of two or more elements returns the whole list, its count in scalar context) is right as far as it goes and does NOT touch this.

PROBE 1 -- evaluated once vs every use (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s507/review/e7-const2.pl):
  my $n; BEGIN { $n = 0 }
  use constant C => ++$n; use constant RND => rand(); use constant T => [1, 2]; use constant H => { a => 1 };
  print C, C, C, " n=$n";                 perl: 111 n=1        PCL: 123 n=3
  RND == RND                              perl: same           PCL: diff
  T == T                                  perl: sameref        PCL: diffref
  push @{+T}, 3; scalar(@{+T})            perl: 3              PCL: 2      <- a constant used as a shared container loses every write
  H->{b} = 2; keys %{+H}                  perl: a,b            PCL: a
PROBE 2 -- a single expression that yields a LIST (e6-sel1.pl rows 28-34; e1-const.pl rows 31, 32):
  use constant R => 1 .. 5;               my @r = R;  perl 5 elements; PCL 1 (emitted as `(p-flipflop-num 0 1 5)`: the range is compiled in SCALAR context, with "Use of uninitialized value $. in numeric eq" on stderr)
  use constant M => map { $_ * 2 } 1 .. 3;            perl (2,4,6); PCL the count/0
  use constant T => (localtime(0))[5, 4];             perl 2 elements; PCL 1
  sub lst { (4, 5) } use constant FC => lst();        perl 2 elements; PCL 1 (lst called in scalar context)
  use constant FA => @arr;  use constant G => grep { $_ } 0, 1, 2;   right today (3; "1 2")
  use constant E => (); my @e = (E, 1);               perl 1 element; PCL 2 -- this row is #2680 (an empty-valued sub in a list), not this task.

THE EMISSION (./pl2cl): `(p-sub pl-X (&rest %_args) (:prototype "") (progn %_args (p-+ 1 2)))` -- the value EXPRESSION is the sub's body, so it runs per call.  perl's constant.pm: `if (@_ == 1) { scalar constant = $_[0] } elsif (@_) { my @list = @_; *name = sub () { @list } } else { *name = sub () { } }`, where @_ is the `use` line's argument list evaluated ONCE in list context at compile time.

FIX SHAPE (a design item, not a filler -- it changes every constant's emission; site Pl/Parser.pm `_process_constant` / `_compile_constant_value`):
  - a LITERAL value (number, string, a foldable arithmetic expression of literals) keeps today's shape -- it is its own once-evaluated value, and the fast path the codegen may inline;
  - anything else: evaluate the value expression ONCE, in LIST context, at the `use` point (the same eval-when the p-sub form already sits in, so a later BEGIN block sees it), into a cell; the sub returns by COUNT: 1 element -> that element in both contexts; 0 -> the empty list / undef; N >= 2 -> the list / the count (s502e's `(if *wantarray* %const-list (length %const-list))` arm, fed from the cell instead of from a re-evaluated vector);
  - the hash form `use constant { A => EXPR, B => EXPR }` takes each value once in SCALAR context (probe: perl evaluates the hash constructor once).
  This is also a SPEED item (Target A): `use constant DEFAULTS => { ... }` allocates a new hash at every use today.
BREAKING CASES to probe: a constant used at compile time by a later `use constant B => A * 2` and by a BEGIN block; a constant read in a string eval and from another package (`Foo::K`, `Foo->K`); `__PACKAGE__->can('NAME')->()`; a module-mode unit (`use`d file) and the script cache -- the once-evaluated value must be computed at LOAD of the cached emission, never baked into the cached text; `use constant NOW => time` across a warm cache; constants whose value captures a lexical (`my $x; BEGIN { $x = 5 } use constant X5 => $x`).
Measure first: how many `use constant` values in the corpus + lib + the everyday programs are non-literal (grep the emission for `(:prototype "")` bodies that are not self-evaluating) -- that is the population the change touches.
subject: SILENT WRONG (found by a s507 review probe, PRE-EXISTING on main 2e71d4aa): `use constant NAME => EXPR` re-evaluates EXPR at EVERY USE and in the USER's context; perl evaluates it ONCE, at the `use`, in LIST context -- `use constant T => [1, 2]` is a FRESH array each use (`push @{+T}, 3` is lost, `T == T` is false), `use constant START => time` moves, `use constant R => 1 .. 5` is a flip-flop, `=> map {...}` / a slice / a call returning a list gives a scalar
